title: Rollback Why-Trace Annotator Prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a lightweight, auditable 'Why' trace annotator that surfaces annotated telemetry context for canary/A-B rollouts and supports rapid rehearsal and rollback reasoning. The feature is a read/write overlay in the Rollouts Console timeline that lets engineers, PMs, and SREs attach structured rationale, evidence links, and severity tags to a traffic shift. These annotations should be searchable, immutable in the audit log once committed, and exportable as runbook snippets for incident playbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype includes overlay timeline with stacked metrics (error rate, p95 latency, throughput, cost) and annotation composer
Annotation composer supports template selection, free-text notes, severity tag, and links to external dashboards/PRs
Annotations are saved to the audit log and appear in the rollout event timeline as immutable entries after commit
Prototype demonstrates replay controls: jump-to-metric timestamp, compare variant lanes, and show annotated snapshots
Design handoff includes component spec, accessibility notes, keyboard shortcuts, and API contract sketch for engineering
Three internal usability sessions (design+eng+se) completed with recorded feedback and prioritized changes
design_notes: Primary surface is a contextual overlay tied to a single rollout event. The overlay has three panes: left - variant selector + quick stats; center - metric timeline with scrubber and stacked annotations; right - annotation composer and historical note list. Composer templates include: 'Spike in 5xx', 'Cost regression', 'Inference quality drop', 'Data skew suspicion'. Each annotation supports one or more evidence links and optional GitHub/Grafana autofill. When a user commits an annotation as 'Official Rationale' we show a confirmation modal and persist the entry to the rollout audit log with user, timestamp, and diff snapshot. The overlay should gracefully degrade on mobile; primary interactions are desktop-first.
decisions: Start with four canonical metrics: error_rate, p95_latency, throughput, and cost. Keep embeddings quality and hallucination metrics for a later phase.
Annotations are editable drafts until 'commit as rationale' is clicked; committed annotations are immutable and recorded in the audit log.
Role gating: only users with 'release-approver' role can mark an annotation as 'Official Rationale' (security review required).
Telemetry links will use deep-linking to Grafana dashboards by default; design will allow custom link templates per org in later release.
